title: Inflation and behaviour: real return, paper loss, recency bias, FOMO
objectives: Explain real return and why “safe” money can still lose value.
Name recency bias and FOMO and how each pushes clients to act.
body_md:
Compounding means earning returns on past returns, so growth speeds up over time: ₹10,000 a month for 20 years at an assumed 12% is about ₹1 crore on ₹24 lakh invested (illustrative). Inflation shrinks what money can buy: at 6% inflation, ₹1 lakh of expenses today becomes about ₹1.8 lakh in 10 years. Real return is return after inflation: a 7% FD with 6% inflation is about 1% real, before tax. The risk-free rate (usually government securities or T-bills) anchors Sharpe-ratio maths. A paper loss is not real until you sell. Recency bias assumes what happened lately will continue; FOMO rushes in because others are making money.

| Term | Plain meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compounding | Earning returns on past returns, so growth speeds up over time | ₹10,000 a month for 20 years at an assumed 12% ≈ ₹1 crore, on ₹24 lakh invested (illustrative) |
| Inflation | The rise in prices that shrinks what money can buy | At 6% inflation, ₹1 lakh of expenses today becomes about ₹1.8 lakh in 10 years |
| Real return | Return after inflation | 7% FD with 6% inflation ≈ 1% real return, before tax |
| Risk-free rate | Return on the safest option, usually government securities or T-bills | Used to calculate the Sharpe ratio |
| Paper loss / paper gain | A fall or rise in value that is not real until you sell | A 15% dip is a paper loss; selling makes it real |
| Recency bias | Assuming what happened lately will continue | "Small caps gave 40% last year, so they'll do it again" |
| FOMO | Fear of missing out: rushing in because others are making money | Buying a hot NFO because a friend did |

> **Investor takeaway:** Inflation is the silent risk. Money that is “safe” but earns less than inflation is quietly losing value.
example: ₹10,000 a month for 20 years at an assumed 12% a year: about ₹1 crore from ₹24 lakh invested — illustrative, not a forecast.
say: “Safe” money earning less than inflation is losing value.
A 15% dip is a paper loss; selling makes it real.
never: A fixed deposit always beats inflation.
Last year's best performer will repeat next year.
